skill.name: verification-before-completion
skill.description: Requires fresh verification evidence before claiming work is complete, fixed, passing, or ready for review.
skill.summary: Requires agents to verify work with current evidence before making completion claims.
skill.author: DYAI2025

content.value_statement: Teams lose time when assistants claim work is done without fresh evidence. This skill forces verification commands and evidence checks before completion claims.
actual_capabilities: Requires fresh verification before success or completion claims.
Prompts agents to identify the command that proves each claim.
Requires reading full command output, exit code, and failure counts.
Distinguishes tests, lint, build, bug fixes, and requirements checks.
Requires independent review of delegated agent results through diffs and verification.
limitations: Does not run commands by itself; the host agent must execute them.
Does not define project-specific test or build commands.
Cannot prove correctness beyond the selected verification evidence.
May slow status updates when full verification is expensive.

use_cases.title: Confirm a Code Fix
use_cases.description: Run the command that proves a bug fix works before reporting completion.

use_cases.title: Prepare Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Verify tests, builds, and requirement checklists before creating or approving a pull request.

use_cases.title: Validate Regression Coverage
use_cases.description: Check that a regression test fails before the fix and passes after the fix.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Simple Fix
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner verification before reporting a small change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Before you say this fix is complete, identify the command that proves it, run it fresh, read the full output, and report the result with evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Check Pull Request Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate verification before opening a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify this branch for pull request readiness. Run the relevant tests and build, review the requirements, and report only claims supported by fresh output.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Regression Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced bug-fix verification with red-green evidence.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use red-green verification for this regression. Show that the test fails without the fix, passes with the fix, and supports the completion claim.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Delegated Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced verification after another agent reports success.
prompt_templates.prompt: Do not trust the delegated success report alone. Inspect the diff, identify the required verification commands, run them fresh, and report the actual state.

output_examples.input: I fixed the failing login test. Verify before completion.
output_examples.output: Ran the targeted login test and read the full output. The test now passes, so the fix is verified for that scenario.

output_examples.input: Before creating the pull request, confirm readiness.
output: Tests passed with no failures in the fresh run.
The build completed successfully with exit code zero.
The requirements checklist matches the implemented changes.

output_examples.input: A subagent says the task is done. Check it.
output_examples.output: Reviewed the diff and ran the relevant verification. The reported success is supported by current evidence, with no unverified completion claims.

best_practices: Run verification in the current conversation before making a completion claim.
Match each claim to the command or checklist that proves it.
Report failures and gaps directly when evidence does not support success.
anti_patterns: Claiming work should pass because the change looks correct.
Using a lint result as proof that a build or test suite passes.
Trusting another agent success report without checking the diff and evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the agent to choose and run the right verification commands.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before any claim that work is complete, fixed, passing, or ready for review.

faq.question: Can it replace project test documentation?
faq.answer: No. It depends on the project to provide the correct test, build, and review commands.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: How does it handle failed verification?
faq.answer: It requires the agent to report the actual status with evidence instead of claiming success.

faq.question: Is this only for software tests?
faq.answer: No. It also applies to builds, requirements, delegated work, and any completion claim.
